macro.narrative: Thursday 10 Sep was a genuine hot-PPI risk-off day layered on top of an already-two-sided setup. August PPI was in-line on the closely-watched monthly headline (+0.4% m/m, matching consensus) but ran hot on annual/core terms (+5.4% y/y, roughly 0.1pt above consensus; core +0.3% m/m/+4.7% y/y unchanged), with over three-quarters of the gain traced to final-demand energy (+4.2%, diesel alone +24.1% m/m) -- itself a Hormuz-driven input. Fed hike odds for the Sep 15-16 FOMC jumped from roughly 60% to roughly 70% on CME FedWatch (readings dispersed 48-70% across trackers through the session, a reminder these tools whipsaw intraday). That real-yield repricing hit precious metals hard even though the Hormuz safe-haven case did not break: SLV fell 5.30% to $57.50, GLD -1.73% to $396.36, GDX -3.46%, and single names were hit harder still (Barrick -6.99%, First Majestic -4.86%, Hecla -3.98%, Pan American -4.25%) -- Kitco described the tape as metals 'trading as a rates-and-dollar market, not a clean safe-haven market' right now, compounding profit-taking after gold had just pushed to 10-week highs. The technical picture is genuinely disputed: one dated recap has gold and silver both closing below their 50- and 200-day moving averages with RSI(14) around 29-31 (oversold, a reversal-leaning read), while other coverage frames it as a near-term pullback ahead of an expected Q4 rally with bank gold targets still $4,900-6,000+ into 2027 -- unresolved pending today's CPI. Oil kept spiking on a THIRD, distinct and escalating driver: Iran claimed strikes on 10 vessels overnight into 10 Sep, described in coverage as the largest declared wave of Hormuz shipping attacks since the war began, with the US retaliating under a new 'tanker-for-tanker' policy (CENTCOM: 'if you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost'); Brent pushed toward $108-109 intraday and WTI past $103.88, even as gold sold off the same day -- a clean decoupling of the real-yield trade from the physical-supply-risk trade. The rare-earth basket sold off on a FOURTH, separate catalyst: fresh reporting that a Trump-Xi summit could be scheduled in Washington later in September, perceived by markets as reducing the 'China-decoupling premium' priced into ex-China names (MP -5.49%, USA Rare Earth -4%, REMX -5%, Energy Fuels -6.32%, Lynas -2.71%) -- notably, this happened the SAME day USA Rare Earth broke ground on a $1.2bn South Carolina magnet facility, and China's actual export-control posture has not visibly eased, so the move reads as a repricing of summit optimism rather than a change in underlying fundamentals. US equities fell only modestly (S&P -0.58% to 7591.70, Russell 2000 -1.04%, a 4th straight down session) but VIX spiked 8.38% to 17.84 -- a real vol/index divergence -- and CNN's live Fear&Greed Index fell further to 33/Fear (from 36) while the dedicated crypto Fear&Greed Index held at 69/Greed (up from 66), a widening rather than narrowing sentiment gap. A genuine counter-signal: the dollar (DXY) fell for a fourth straight session despite the higher hike odds, not fully reconciled this run. US breadth: no fresher confirmed reading than Wednesday 9 Sep's baseline could be sourced (StockCharts/Barchart pages returned empty this run) -- given the VIX spike, further deterioration is likely but unverified, so the prior %>50-DMA/NYSE-A-D/McClellan readings are carried forward with that explicit caveat rather than guessed. Weekly EPFR/Lipper fund flows: still no release fresher than the week ended 2 Sep has published (a search hit that looked like a week-ended-9-Sep figure traced to a mis-dated 2025 article and was excluded). Today's (11 Sep) US CPI print -- consensus 3.4% y/y headline, 2.4% y/y core -- is the decisive next data point determining whether the hawkish repricing extends into next week's FOMC or reverses.
